note: Bravo Health (formerly Elder Health), Medicare Advantage plans, Baltimore; acquired by HealthSpring in 2010, the firm's exit line (HealthSpring later became part of Cigna). NEA's first investment is 1994; no source read names the round.

CareerBuilder Inc., online recruiting (Reston VA), listed on Nasdaq in 1999 and bought in 2000 by Tribune and Knight Ridder, which merged it with CareerPath (the firm's exit line; the business later moved to Chicago). NEA's first investment is 1996; no source read names the round.

CardioThoracic Systems, instruments for beating-heart bypass surgery (Cupertino CA); listed on Nasdaq (CTSI) in 1996 and acquired by Guidant in 1999, the firm's exit line. NEA's first investment is 1995; no source read names the round.

Cardiovascular Imaging Systems, intravascular ultrasound catheters (Sunnyvale CA); listed on Nasdaq (CVIS) and acquired by Boston Scientific in 1995, the firm's exit line. NEA's first investment is 1987; no source read names the round.

Carrier Access, telecom access equipment (Boulder CO), listed on Nasdaq in 1998 and acquired by Turin Networks in 2008 (Turin later went to Force10, the firm's exit line), as in the Menlo row. NEA's first investment is 1997; no source read names the round.

Broadview Networks, integrated communications for businesses (Rye Brook NY), founded 1996; Windstream agreed to buy it in April 2017 for $227.5M in cash (Wikipedia). Wikipedia lists NEA among its shareholders with Baker Capital, MCG and others; NEA's first investment is 2005 and no source read names the round.

BridgePoint Medical, catheter systems for chronic total occlusions (Plymouth MN, the Form D address); acquired by Boston Scientific, the firm's exit line. NEA's first investment is 2002 (the firm's own year), which replaces the 2009 entry date on file read off a later Form D; no source read names the round.

Carticept Medical, osteoarthritis and cartilage devices (Alpharetta GA, the Form D address); it went to Cartiva, itself bought by Wright Medical Group (the firm's exit line). NEA's first investment is 2005 (the firm's own year), which replaces the 2010 entry date on file read off a later Form D; no source read names the round.
Cartiva, synthetic cartilage implants (Alpharetta GA, the Form D address); acquired by Wright Medical Group in 2018, the firm's exit line. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Brightkite, location-based social network; the mobile network Limbo acquired it in April 2009 and the combined company filed as Brightkite, Inc. from Burlingame CA (Form D, 2009, Peter Sonsini a director). By December 2011 its apps were pulled and by April 2012 the site was gone (Wikipedia): defunct. No source read names NEA's round.

CareZone, medication and care-management app (San Francisco, the Form D address); Walmart acquired it in 2020, the firm's exit line. The Form D band's Series A entry (2012, Greg Papadopoulos a director) stands.
Burrow, modular furniture sold direct (New York); acquired by Havenly, the firm's exit line, as in the General Catalyst and Y Combinator rows.

Casper Sleep, mattresses (New York). Listed on the NYSE in 2020, taken private by Durational Capital in 2022 (the firm's exit line) and acquired by Carpenter Co. in October 2024 (Wikipedia). The Form D band's Series A entry agrees with Wikipedia: a $13.1M Series A in 2014 with NEA among the investors, after a $1.85M seed.

Care.com, marketplace for family care (Wikipedia: headquartered in Dallas, bought by IAC in February 2020); the IVP row reads Waltham, its home through the IPO, and should align. Its draft S-1 (2013-09-13) lists New Enterprise Associates 13 buying $13.5M of Series C preferred, then Series D and E; Matrix had led the $3.5M Series A in 2007 (Wikipedia). The Series C is the October 2010 Form D round, the firm's first-investment year: Growth.

ChannelAdvisor, e-commerce channel software (Morrisville NC); listed on the NYSE in 2013, acquired by CommerceHub in 2022. Its draft S-1 dates Series A to December 2003, Series B to April 2005, Series B-1 to April 2006 and Series C to April 2007; the investors' rights agreement entered with the Series C purchase defines NEA as New Enterprise Associates 12 and NEA Ventures 2007, and Patrick Kerins joined the board in 2007, the firm's first-investment year: Growth.

The firm's description (nicotinic-receptor drugs for CNS disorders) is Targacept, NEA's 2002 investment, which merged with Catalyst Biosciences in 2015; Catalyst in turn combined with Gyre Therapeutics in 2023 (Nasdaq: GYRE, San Diego, its listing profile). The firm's own listing labels the 2002 entry Growth. Market cap $767.68M as of 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis.com) replaces the $72.6M float on file; still below $1B.

Celcuity, targeted cancer drugs (Minneapolis). NEA joined the May 2022 private placement led by Venrock Healthcare Capital Partners (8-K, 2022-05-16), years after the 2017 listing. Market cap $3.83B as of 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis.com) replaces the $457M float on file: band 1b_plus. The firm labels this entry Public/PIPES: a private placement into an already listed company, which decisions X1 reads as out unless an NEA private round came first; no earlier NEA round is on record, so the membership should be re-judged under X1.

Champions Oncology, preclinical and translational oncology research services; its listing profile gives One University Plaza, Hackensack NJ (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/csbr/company/), with labs in Maryland; the Battery row reads Baltimore and should align. NEA 14 bought in through the March 2015 securities purchase agreement with Battery (8-K, 2015-03-12), when the company already traded. The firm labels this entry Public/PIPES: a private placement into an already listed company, which decisions X1 reads as out unless an NEA private round came first; no earlier NEA round is on record, so the membership should be re-judged under X1.

Cadence Pharmaceuticals, hospital products (San Diego); listed on Nasdaq in 2006, acquired by Mallinckrodt in 2014. NEA joined the February 2009 private placement led by Venrock (8-K, 2009-02-20). The firm labels this entry Public/PIPES: a private placement into an already listed company, which decisions X1 reads as out unless an NEA private round came first; no earlier NEA round is on record, so the membership should be re-judged under X1.

Cascadian Therapeutics (formerly Oncothyreon, Seattle), cancer drugs; acquired by Seattle Genetics in 2018. NEA held 7.9% by October 2016 (proxy), bought as a listed company in 2016, one of the Growth Equity Opportunities 13D issuers (decisions R2). The firm labels this entry Public/PIPES: a private placement into an already listed company, which decisions X1 reads as out unless an NEA private round came first; no earlier NEA round is on record, so the membership should be re-judged under X1.
Cerecor was renamed Avalo Therapeutics (Nasdaq: AVTX) and is now headquartered at 1500 Liberty Ridge Drive, Wayne PA (its listing profile, stockanalysis.com); the Form D address was Baltimore.

Bright Health Group renamed itself NeueHealth and moved its headquarters to Doral FL, as in the Tiger Global row (the Headline row reads Minneapolis, its original home, and should align); in December 2024 NEA agreed to take NeueHealth private, the acquisition on file. Below $1B.

Chelsio Communications, fabless semiconductor company for high-speed Ethernet adapters, privately held and headquartered in Sunnyvale (Wikipedia). Wikipedia lists NEA among its early venture investors, with a Series D in 2006 and a $25M Series E by January 2008, and it still ships products (T7 DPU sampling, 2025); NEA's first investment is 2002 (the firm's own year), which replaces the 2009 entry date on file, and no source read names the round.

Caremark Rx (formerly MedPartners), pharmacy benefit manager, moved from Birmingham to Nashville in 2003 and merged with CVS in 2007 (Wikipedia, CVS Caremark). The firm listed it only in its 2008 and 2013 archive with no investment year, and NEA's one filing is a 13G of 2000-02-11, when MedPartners had been listed since 1995: the stake reads as a listed holding or sale consideration from a portfolio company MedPartners bought (decisions D8, X1), so the membership should be re-judged.

ByteDance (Toutiao, Douyin, TikTok), based in Haidian, Beijing (Wikipedia). Mark: the company's own employee share buyback at $200.41 a share, valuing it at over $330B (The Business Times, from Reuters, 2025-08-27), a priced repurchase by the company; later secondary reports ($480B in a November 2025 share auction, $550B in General Atlantic's proposed 2026 sale) stay out of the figure. Stage: NEA's first investment is 2018, when ByteDance had already raised Series A to E and a pre-IPO round (SoftBank-led, 2018), so any NEA entry, primary or secondary, is Growth; no source read names NEA's round.

BuzzFeed, digital media (New York), listed on Nasdaq (BZFD) through a SPAC in December 2021. NEA's entry is the $15.5M round announced in January 2012 (Wikipedia; Form D first sale 2011-12-23, Patrick Kerins a director), which followed the company's 2008 round and an $8M round filed in 2010: a third institutional round above the era's $15M Series A ceiling, Growth. NEA also led the $19.3M round of January 2013 (Wikipedia).

Change (GetChange Corp., getchange.io), donation APIs linking companies to charities. The firm's own listing labels its 2022 first investment Seed. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, the company's name with donation API and raise words): no round found, below $1B. Its site gives no headquarters city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

CHAOS Industries, radar and sensing for drone and missile detection and defense networking (Los Angeles, Crunchbase News). Crunchbase News (2025-05-02): Accel and NEA co-led the $275M Series C at a $2B valuation, after a $145M Series B; NEA's first-investment year is 2025, so the entry is the Series C, Growth. Mark: the $510M round led by Valor Equity Partners at a $4.5B valuation (Tectonic, 2025-11-14). The 8VC and Accel rows read below $1B and should align; the General Catalyst and Lightspeed rows named Chaos are a different company (a New York crypto firm).

Candy Digital, licensed sports and entertainment NFTs, founded in 2021 by Fanatics with Galaxy Digital and VaynerMedia (New York); the Italian country on file came from a one-word name match (the appliance maker Candy) and is replaced. Sportcal (2021-10-22): a $100M Series A at a $1.5B valuation led by Insight Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund 2, with NEA participating, the firm's first-investment year. Futureverse acquired it in April 2025 (Axios) and the Tad Smith family bought it in 2026 (National Law Review): acquired, below $1B.

Ceramic.ai, infrastructure to train and deploy AI models faster, founded by former Google VP Anna Patterson. Tech Funding News (2025-03-05): a $12M seed led by NEA with IBM, Samsung Next and Earthshot; the firm's listing labels it Seed with a 2024 first investment. The entry is inside 24 months, censored. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, 'Ceramic AI raises'): no later round, below $1B. No source read states a headquarters city.

Built Robotics, autonomy kits for construction equipment, now solar pile-driving robots (San Francisco). A $33M Series B in 2019 and a $64M Series C in April 2022 (TechCrunch) with no valuation disclosed; below $1B, as in the Tiger Global row. The Form D band's Series A entry (2017, Forest Baskett a director) stands.

Cardioxyl Pharmaceuticals, nitroxyl donors for heart failure (Chapel Hill NC, the Form D address); acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2015, the firm's exit line. The firm's own listing labels its 2006 first investment Seed, which replaces the 2009 entry date on file read off a later Form D; later offerings of $9M (2009), $15M (2010) and $28M (2012) are unnamed. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Canopy, practice management and tax resolution software for accounting firms (Lehi UT, the Form D address), still operating (CPA Practice Advisor, 2025-2026) and raising (a $36.5M Form D offering in 2025); no valuation on record, below $1B. The a16z, General Catalyst and Y Combinator rows named Canopy are different companies. The Form D band's Series A entry (2015, Chetan Puttagunta a director) stands.

Catalog Technologies, DNA-based data storage (Boston). Its domain now redirects to Biomemory, whose site says 'Biomemory acquires key assets from Catalog', adding a production and R&D footprint in Boston: an asset sale, acquired with Biomemory (Paris) as successor. NEA's first investment is 2017; no source read names the round.

Broadly, reviews and customer messaging software for local businesses. Its site (Broadly Inc.) is live and gives 951 Yamato Road, Boca Raton FL as its address; the company began in the San Francisco Bay Area. NEA's first investment is 2015; Google News carries no round of the company under its generic name, so the round is not on record.

Brenig Therapeutics, brain-penetrant small molecules for Parkinson's disease (LRRK2) and neuroinflammation (NLRP3). Pulse 2.0 (2024-07-25): a $65M Series A led by NEA with existing backers OrbiMed, Torrey Pines Investment and BioGeneration Ventures; NEA's first-investment year is 2024, so the entry is the Series A, and the Form D band's Growth (read from the $65M size) is disputed; the entry date stays the Form D first sale. The Form D and site give only a Dover DE registered-agent address, so no city is placed. No valuation disclosed.

Centralize, AI relationship intelligence for enterprise sales (San Francisco), Y Combinator Winter 2024. Crunchbase News (2026-07-29): a $15M Series A led by NEA with Salesforce Ventures and Y Combinator, after a $4M seed, $19M in total; NEA's first-investment year is 2026, so the entry is the Series A. No valuation disclosed; momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News): no later round, below $1B. The Y Combinator row is the same company and agrees.

Cardurion Pharmaceuticals, cardiovascular drugs (Burlington MA, the Form D address). NEA's entry is the $260M Series B of July 2024 (Fierce Biotech, BioPharma Dive), which agrees with the Form D band's Growth; Edward Mathers joined the board. No valuation disclosed, below $1B.

Cathay Industrial Biotech, bio-based long-chain dicarboxylic acids and polyamides (Shanghai). Its 2011 F-1 (withdrawn) lists New Enterprise Associates 12 among the preferred investors; the company listed on the Shanghai STAR Market in 2020 as Cathay Biotech (688065). Market cap CNY 27.85B as of 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis.com): CNY 27.85B @ ECB 2026-09-30 (CNY/EUR 7.613, EUR/USD 1.1355) = $4.15B, band 1b_plus. The firm's own listing labels its 2007 entry Growth.

Causes, online activism platform co-founded by Sean Parker (San Francisco); it became part of Brigade Media (the firm's exit line), and Countable Corporation acquired Causes and Brigade in 2019 (Wikipedia). Wikipedia names NEA among its investors with Founders Fund and the Case Foundation; NEA's first investment is 2010 and no source read names the round.

Catalytic, no-code workflow automation (Chicago, the Form D address); acquired by PagerDuty in 2022, the firm's exit line and Built In Chicago's list of 2022 acquisitions. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

CenterBeam, outsourced IT management for mid-sized enterprises (Sunnyvale, the Form D address); EarthLink bought it for $22M in June 2013 (Data Center Dynamics), the firm's archived exit line. NEA's first investment is 1999 (the firm's own year), which replaces the 2013 entry date on file read off a late Form D; no source read names the round.

Centrexion Therapeutics, non-opioid pain drugs (Boston, the Form D address). It withdrew its IPO in May 2021 and its knee pain drug failed two Phase III studies in 2022 (Endpoints), but it kept raising privately (Form D offerings of $30M in 2022 and $12.9M in 2024): private, below $1B. The Form D band's Growth entry (2017, Sara Nayeem a director) agrees with the $67M round of January 2018 (Fierce Biotech).

CHARM Therapeutics, AI-designed small molecules, lead program a next-generation menin inhibitor for AML (London, EU-Startups 2025-09-02). NEA's entry is the $80M Series B of September 2025, co-led with SR One (Snell & Wilmer; Pulse 2.0), which agrees with the Form D band's Growth; a $50M Series A came in 2022 (TechCrunch) and NVIDIA's NVentures invested in 2023. No valuation disclosed, below $1B. The General Catalyst row reads unknown and US; this London company is private.

Cardionomic, catheter-based neuromodulation for acute decompensated heart failure (Forest Lake MN, the Form D address), Ali Behbahani on the board. NEA's first investment is 2010 (the firm's own year), which replaces the 2015 entry date on file read off the company's first Form D ($21.8M, 2015); later offerings of $9.6M (2018), $16.8M (2020) and $11.5M (2021) are unnamed, and no source read names NEA's round.
